title: Standardize SDK release pipelines and artifact signing for Python/TS/Go
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Create a unified, auditable release pipeline for Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) that produces signed, provenance-rich artifacts and automates publishing to PyPI, npm, and Go module registries. This ticket covers CI configuration (GitHub Actions templates), deterministic changelog generation, version bumping rules, artifact signing (sigstore/cosign + optional GPG), attestations (in-toto/TUF style metadata), and rollback procedures.

Scope:
- Provide reusable GitHub Actions workflows for build/test/package/sign and publish for each language.
- Integrate cosign for container and archive signing and Rekor transparency logs for immutability.
- Produce machine-readable artifact metadata (SBOM / attestation) linked to commits and release tags.
- Define semantic versioning policy for SDKs, automated changelog from merged PRs, and release notes templates.
- Implement gated release jobs that require passing CI, branch protection, and an approver.
- Add Canary/pulsing releases for major changes (e.g., new streaming API surface) with automated rollback hook.

Non-goals: migrating old releases, changing public registry accounts, or implementing a full TUF repo server (we will use sigstore + Rekor for first-phase supply chain guarantees).

Why now: Multiple incidents where packages were published without signed metadata and inconsistent versioning caused customer confusion and slowed rollbacks. This is aligned with Compliance roadmap for stronger supply-chain guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: One reusable GitHub Actions workflow template per language (python/npm/go) in .github/workflows/release-templates
Artifacts signed with cosign + Rekor entry produced for each release
Publish job successfully pushes to test PyPI/npm registry and Go proxy for a tagged commit in a staging repo
Generated release notes and changelog entries from merged PR titles and labels
A documented manual rollback procedure validated in a dry-run
Security sign-off recorded in the ticket comments
tasks: Draft workflow templates and add to central repo (eng/release-workflows)
Wire up repository secrets and OIDC-based sigstore credentials
Add unit/integration steps that build, run SDK tests, and create artifacts (sdist/wheel, tarball, npm pack, go mod)
Add attestation/metadata generation step (SBOM or simple JSON with commit, deps, build flags)
Create canary release job that only publishes to staged registries and notifies #releases
Document versioning policy and update CONTRIBUTING.md
risks: Publish tokens leak risk — mitigated by OIDC-based short-lived creds and least-privilege roles
Language-specific packaging edge-cases (PEP517 wheels, npm package exports, go modules) — allocate dedicated testing matrix
Developer friction on signing step — provide one-click `gh release create` helper using stored workflows

implementation_notes: Use GitHub OIDC to mint ephemeral GCP/AWS creds for publishing; avoid long-lived registry tokens where possible
Cosign will sign built archives (wheel/sdist, tarball for go, tgz for npm) and upload signature alongside artifact or attach as release asset
For PyPI, use test.pypi.org for dry runs. For npm, use npm test registry and ephemeral scope. For Go, validate via GOPRIVATE proxy and public proxy for public modules
Versioning: adopt conventional commits for automated changelog; bump patch/minor/major based on PR labels (release-tooling will infer)
Changelog: generate using github-release-notes with template that highlights API surface changes (streaming, retry defaults, client config)
Rollback: create a documented script to mark releases as yanked (PyPI) and unpublish from staging registries and create follow-up tickets for published packages that require revoke
notes_for_reviewers: Please review the proposed GitHub Actions templates in eng/release-workflows and flag any blocking packaging concerns.
Security: confirm that the sigstore keyless workflow and Rekor configuration meet compliance controls (we will share Rekor root certs in private thread).
QA: validate canary publish to test registries and confirm consumers can fetch the canary module via go proxy and npm install from test registry.
